# State SOTP - Segment G9

Phase 6 identified the State Startup Nodal Department as the only ACT NOW segment: urgency 4, revenue potential 4. It is also the buyer that Phases 0-5 never modelled, because state portals were invisible to a competitor scan that looked for commercial vendors.

## Why it is sized separately

G9 is not an institution. It is a government buyer with a different decision chain, a different contract vehicle and a different clock. Mixing it into the institutional SAM or SOM would corrupt both, so it gets a sum-of-the-parts and its own falsifier.

## The parts

| Component | Value | Provenance |
|---|---|---|
| Buyers | 34 States and UTs | T1_DOCUMENTED (SRF 5.0 participating) |
| Deal shape | portal replacement / platform contract | MODELLED |
| ACV | Rs 2,500,000 - Rs 8,000,000 | **PRIOR** |
| Attainable over 3 yrs | 3-8 of 34 | **PRIOR** |
| Indicative value | Rs 0.8-6.4 crore | PRIOR |
| Forcing event | SRF evaluation cycle; results published each January | T1_DOCUMENTED |

## Honest labelling

The ACV band is **PRIOR, not evidence.** Analyst range. No state portal procurement value is published anywhere. Anchored on the observation that a state portal must serve a whole-state ecosystem and is a scored national deliverable - but this is PRIOR, not evidence.

The attainable range is **Zero to eight of 34 over three years. A state portal decision is a ministerial one; it is not a founder-led sales motion and it does not compound the way institutional licences do.**

> Sized separately and on the PRIOR tier. The whole point of segment G9 is that it is the only ACT NOW quadrant - but ACT NOW means the forcing event is strong, not that the sale is easy. Treat this as an option, not a plan.

## What would make this a plan instead of an option

One conversation with one Nodal Officer. That has not happened. Phase 6 also recorded that no Emerging-tier state report was obtainable, so the states most likely to be buying have published no evidence about what they buy.
